flags: minor: distractors A/C/D are easy to eliminate; D ('indifferent to') is a nonsense choice nobody would pick
S031-01.notes: Exact reproduction with only hidden systems changed = faithful to the original. A contradicts; C is unsupported; D cannot describe a building's relationship to a design.

flags: minor: the colon clause ('only if...') nearly defines 'conditional', so the item is close to a lookup
S031-02.notes: Taking effect only if a requirement is met is the definition of a conditional offer. None of the others is supported.

flags: minor: B ('proves') and A are overstated in an obvious way; D is the only hedged/negative choice, which cues it
S031-03.notes: The pollen evidence gives another possible cause, so the timing alone cannot establish human responsibility. B overreaches (it proves nothing); A has no support; C contradicts 'same time'.

S031-04.notes: If crows also avoid an identical park that was never used for trapping, the avoidance points to features of the park rather than learned danger. A fits fading memory; B supports socially transmitted danger association; D restates the premise and if anything supports the hypothesis. The trap is D, since it mentions park features.

flags: minor: A is the only choice that compares across seasons, which is the comparison the conclusion needs, so it is easy to spot
S031-05.notes: Dry: 96-75=21; rainy: 97-93=4. Both differences check out. B, C and D are true but do not show the difference is larger in the dry season.

flags: minor: D closely paraphrases Text 2's last sentence ('recording what was thought to be known... more than a way of marking danger'), so the item is close to a lookup
S031-06.notes: The historian says the creatures recorded supposed knowledge rather than marking danger. A agrees with Text 1; B contradicts the claim that the creatures were drawn from natural-history books and believed in; C is never discussed. The claim about historical cartography is plausible (it resembles Chet Van Duzer's work).

S031-07.notes: The audience is unfamiliar with qanats, so the choice must say what a qanat is as well as state an advantage. B does both. A gives the advantage but no definition (the trap). C and D give no advantage.

flags: minor: factual check: Hunga Tonga released about 146 Tg of water vapor and little SO2, and early papers did suggest a temporary warming. Later analyses found a slight net cooling, but 'some scientists suggest' is accurate
S031-08.notes: 'Instead' sets the large release of water vapor against the small release of SO2. B is wrong because the two are not similar; C is wrong because releasing little SO2 did not cause the water vapor release; D is wrong because the sentence is not a specification of the previous one.

flags: minor: Reykjavik lies just south of the Arctic Circle; calling it a stop on an 'Arctic voyage' is acceptable
S031-09.notes: A series whose items contain commas is separated with semicolons, matching the '; and Iqaluit' that follows. A gives an inconsistent series; B uses a colon wrongly; D omits needed punctuation.

S031-10.notes: The subject 'Sylvia Earle' needs a finite main verb after the nonrestrictive clause. Only 'founded' supplies one. A, B and C leave the sentence a fragment. Facts check out: Earle founded Mission Blue in 2009 and has led 100+ expeditions with 7,000+ hours underwater.
